review.value: Behavior Analysis Services may be delivered and billed in the recipient's home (POS 12), school (POS 03), community (POS 99), and clinic/office (POS 11) settings.

review.source: Florida_Medicaid_Behavior_Analysis_Services_Coverage_Policy.pdf
review.value: To support billing Behavior Analysis Services, the Florida Medicaid record must contain the original referral information, a behavior assessment and behavior plan signed by the Lead Analyst and the recipient's parent or guardian (including reason for referral, history, clinical interview, assessment procedures/results, targets, goals and objectives with baseline and mastery criteria, generalization, caregiver training, units requested, supervision, care coordination, transition, crisis and discharge plans), progress data with tables and graphs plus narrative justification for reauthorization, and session notes signed and dated by the rendering practitioner, in addition to the general recordkeeping elements of Rule 59G-1.054, F.A.C.

review.source: Florida_Medicaid_Behavior_Analysis_Services_Coverage_Policy.pdf
review.value: Florida Medicaid recipients under age 21 requiring medically necessary behavior analysis services must have behavior that impairs their ability to perform a major life activity, expressed through behaviors in categories including safety, communication, self-stimulating, self-care, or other behaviors affecting treatment complexity.

review.source: Florida_Medicaid_Behavior_Analysis_Services_Coverage_Policy.pdf
review.value: Behavior Analysis Services require prior authorization under Florida Medicaid, with services covered up to 40 hours per week as indicated in the recipient's prior-authorized behavior plan and authorization renewed at least every six months based on a reassessment and updated behavior plan.

standard_requirements.statement: Florida Medicaid recipients under age 21 requiring medically necessary behavior analysis services must have behavior that impairs their ability to perform a major life activity, expressed through behaviors in categories including safety, communication, self-stimulating, self-care, or other behaviors affecting treatment complexity.

To support billing Behavior Analysis Services, the Florida Medicaid record must contain the original referral information, a behavior assessment and behavior plan signed by the Lead Analyst and the recipient's parent or guardian (including reason for referral, history, clinical interview, assessment procedures/results, targets, goals and objectives with baseline and mastery criteria, generalization, caregiver training, units requested, supervision, care coordination, transition, crisis and discharge plans), progress data with tables and graphs plus narrative justification for reauthorization, and session notes signed and dated by the rendering practitioner, in addition to the general recordkeeping elements of Rule 59G-1.054, F.A.C.
Behavior Analysis Services may be delivered and billed in the recipient's home (POS 12), school (POS 03), community (POS 99), and clinic/office (POS 11) settings.

Behavior Analysis Services require prior authorization under Florida Medicaid, with services covered up to 40 hours per week as indicated in the recipient's prior-authorized behavior plan and authorization renewed at least every six months based on a reassessment and updated behavior plan.

Under Florida Medicaid rule 59G-4.031, Behavioral Health Community Support Services have no service-specific authorization (prior authorization) criteria in the fee-for-service delivery system, but coverage is limited to 1,920 units per recipient, per fiscal year, with psychosocial rehabilitation and clubhouse service units combined counting toward that limit.
